summary: Two material changes since the prior snapshot: the Bank of Japan raised its policy rate 25 bp to 1.25%, extending the global tightening cycle after the Fed hike; and Hormuz commodity traffic remained severely impaired while three LNG vessels reappeared outside the strait, a tentative partial de-escalation signal rather than normalization. No new U.S., Taiwan or China official macro release superseded the prior snapshot.

Taiwan's unchanged 2.0% policy rate remains comparatively supportive domestically, but persistent Hormuz impairment, Russian refined-product disruption, high oil prices and dollar strength remain material risks to margins, FX and valuation multiples.

key_drivers.name: BOJ raises policy rate to 1.25%
key_drivers.observed: BOJ published a September 18 change in its money-market guideline; Reuters reports a 25-bp increase to 1.25%, the highest in 31 years, on a 7-2 vote.
key_drivers.interpretation: Extends global tightening and adds discount-rate pressure, although the yen weakened because guidance was less hawkish than markets expected.

key_drivers.name: Hormuz remains severely impaired; LNG vessels reappear
key_drivers.observed: Reuters/Kpler reported four commodity-vessel transits Thursday versus six Wednesday and a 10-day average of 16; three LNG vessels reappeared outside the strait after several days.
key_drivers.interpretation: The LNG movement is a tentative de-escalation signal, but traffic remains far below normal and does not remove Taiwan energy, freight or insurance risk.

key_drivers.name: Saudi supply fears ease at margin
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported oil prices fell for a third straight session Friday as fears of immediate Saudi supply disruption eased.
key_drivers.interpretation: Near-term crude tail risk has declined from the week's peak, but the East-West Pipeline impairment and Hormuz bottleneck keep the broader energy shock active.

key_risks: Fed and BOJ tightening can keep global discount rates and funding costs elevated.
Hormuz traffic remains severely below normal despite tentative LNG movement.
Saudi East-West Pipeline damage and Russian refinery outages keep oil/refined-product tail risks elevated.
U.S.-Russia/Iran sanctions legislation remains a conditional trade and energy shock pending implementation.
Exact VIX, copper, USD/TWD and U.S. Treasury closes remain stale in this semantic snapshot.
